supported.boundaries: Vowel or ㄹ stem: attached ㄹ + 라치면; other coda: 을라치면. Existing ㄷ/ㅂ/ㅅ irregular recovery remains available.
supported.composition: Auxiliary verb groups, negative verbs, lexical 있다/계시다 and polite 요. Polite and irregular extra heads are marked composition probes rather than quoted examples.
supported.excluded: Recovered past/modal/retrospective stacks, explicit copulas, derived 답다 adjective and represented adjective auxiliaries do not inherit the verb ending.
supported.dictionary: Known lexical adjective entries conflict, except source-attested 있다. The requirement follows 지+않다/아니하다/못하다, with the conflict owned by the lexical entry and pointing to the later ending index. Other auxiliaries, suffixes and copulas reset that dependency. Each homonym is assessed independently; unknown evidence remains unknown.

observations.reason: KAIST tags 있다 as adjective in an existential sentence. KRDict also illustrates the surface. Do not discard that lexical entry based on the broader verb-only note.

An intermediate implementation checked only direct lexical attachment and allowed the lexical adjective class to disappear through negation. Five additional policy cases and explicit conflict ownership/unknown-evidence tests cover the correction; 좋아질라치면 tests class reset.

Raw output preserves hypothetical stem identities such as 먹었다+을라치면, 의사이다+을라치면 and nested joined heads. These do not bypass the tested recovered prefinal/copula roles, and are not certified by required candidate matches. Full raw additions and the validity review queue are retained.
Auxiliary chains may be analyzed in joined input; this is not automatic spacing repair. Canonical 을라치면 displays normalized forms after vowel stems, with both source allomorphs available.

Primary NIKL spelling guide, printed p. 59, gives both forms; current probes have no expected predicate path. KRDict 85762/85772 define the ending separately from restrictive particle 밖에, with verb/adjective/copula and honorific/past licenses.

The browser defaults to the be-deaf 먹다 homonym. Both verb homonyms remain candidates and the eating sense is available in dictionary entries; morphology does not choose the intended contextual sense. Auxiliary glosses can also remain transliterations. Contextual ranking stays outside this batch.
